topic.title: Learning through Interaction and World Models
topic.overview: An agent can learn from what happens after it acts, not just from expert demonstrations. This topic studies experience-driven policies, models of environment dynamics, planning, skill discovery, and exploratory behavior. World models provide a way to relate actions to future states, while the training signal may come from rewards, observed transitions, or reflection on mistakes.
topic.whyItMatters: Interaction exposes an agent to situations that demonstrations may omit, but collecting long trajectories or reliable rewards can be expensive. Different approaches trade off direct experience, simulated prediction, and supervision from outcomes; improvements in one environment do not establish general-purpose autonomy.
topic.evolution: A 1991 temporal-difference study learns backgammon evaluation through self-play. More recent representatives examine learned planning and open-ended embodied environments. In 2026, early-experience learning uses agent-generated transitions without reward signals, studying implicit world modeling and self-reflection across eight environments as preparation for more effective subsequent learning.
openQuestions: When do learned world models help exploration rather than reinforce mistaken expectations?
How can agents learn useful skills from interactions that lack reliable rewards?

papers.tldr: A graph-based chess architecture learns playing strength faster in the reported comparisons and transfers through fine-tuning between board sizes.

papers.title: Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model
papers.tldr: New automaton-based evaluations reveal incoherent implicit world models that existing diagnostics miss in game playing, logic, and navigation.

papers.title: Evidence of Learned Look-Ahead in a Chess-Playing Neural Network
papers.tldr: Analysis of Leela Chess Zero finds causally important future-move representations, providing evidence that its neural network has learned look-ahead.

papers.title: FactorSim: Generative Simulation via Factorized Representation
papers.tldr: FactorSim generates complete simulation code from language using a factored representation that reduces context dependence during generation.

papers.title: GAVEL: Generating Games via Evolution and Language Models
papers.tldr: GAVEL combines language models and evolutionary computation to mutate and recombine game code, generating interesting games beyond the dataset’s existing rule coverage.

papers.title: Grounded Answers for Multi-agent Decision-making Problem through Generative World Model
papers.tldr: A language-guided world model trains coordinated policies and generates visual answers grounded in simulated interactions and learned rewards.

papers.title: Implicit Curriculum in Procgen Made Explicit
papers.tldr: C-Procgen exposes a gradual easy-to-hard learning progression that suggests an implicit curriculum during multi-level reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Improving Environment Novelty Quantification for Effective Unsupervised Environment Design
papers.tldr: CENIE improves automated curricula by combining regret with novelty measured from the student's previous state-action coverage.

papers.title: JaxMARL: Multi-Agent RL Environments and Algorithms in JAX
papers.tldr: JaxMARL accelerates multi-agent reinforcement-learning environments and algorithms with JAX and introduces the flexible SMAX benchmark.

papers.title: KALM: Knowledgeable Agents by Offline Reinforcement Learning from Large Language Model Rollouts
papers.tldr: KALM trains agents offline on language-model-generated rollouts, improving success on novel robotic goals in its reported experiments.

papers.title: Learning Human-like Representations to Enable Learning Human Values
papers.tldr: Human-like representations support safe exploration and better generalization when agents learn human values in personalization experiments.

papers.title: Learning to Assist Humans without Inferring Rewards
papers.tldr: Contrastive successor representations help assistive agents increase human control without first inferring human rewards.

papers.title: Learning to Cooperate with Humans using Generative Agents
papers.tldr: GAMMA generates diverse training partners from a learned latent model and improves coordination with real humans in Overcooked.

papers.title: Maia-2: A Unified Model for Human-AI Alignment in Chess
papers.tldr: Maia-2 uses skill-aware attention in a unified chess model to better match human play across expertise levels.

papers.title: Mars: Situated Inductive Reasoning in an Open-World Environment
papers.tldr: Mars tests whether agents can discover unfamiliar environmental rules through interaction, with reflection-based induction improving performance on the challenging benchmark.

papers.title: No Regrets: Investigating and Improving Regret Approximations for Curriculum Discovery
papers.tldr: Prioritizing environments an agent can sometimes solve improves curriculum learning over regret approximations that favor already-mastered tasks.

papers.title: Opponent Modeling with In-context Search
papers.tldr: OMIS combines in-context opponent modeling with decision-time search to improve adaptation and stability against unfamiliar, changing agents.

papers.title: Policy Learning from Tutorial Books via Understanding, Rehearsing and Introspecting
papers.tldr: A three-stage framework turns tutorial-book knowledge into imagined trajectories and then policy networks, showing effective game play without real training data.

papers.title: PUZZLES: A Benchmark for Neural Algorithmic Reasoning
papers.tldr: PUZZLES provides 40 adjustable logic puzzles and baseline evaluations for studying reasoning and generalization in reinforcement learning.

papers.title: RL-GPT: Integrating Reinforcement Learning and Code-as-policy
papers.tldr: RL-GPT combines hierarchical coding agents with reinforcement learning to improve efficiency on embodied tasks, including Minecraft and designated MineDojo evaluations.

papers.title: Skill-aware Mutual Information Optimisation for Zero-shot Generalisation in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Skill-aware context learning improves reported zero-shot reinforcement learning generalization and makes context encoders more robust to reduced sample availability.

papers.title: STL: Still Tricky Logic (for System Validation, Even When Showing Your Work)

papers.title: Using Unity to Help Solve Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: U3 combines XLand 2.0 and Unity into an open-source toolkit for rapidly building varied 3D reinforcement-learning environments.

papers.title: WorldCoder, a Model-Based LLM Agent: Building World Models by Writing Code and Interacting with the Environment
papers.tldr: WorldCoder learns editable Python world models from interaction, showing efficiency and transfer benefits in gridworlds and task planning.

papers.title: A Causal World Model Underlying Next Token Prediction: Exploring GPT in a Controlled Environment
papers.tldr: In controlled game environments, GPT’s ability to generate legal moves is associated with confidently encoded causal structure in attention.

papers.title: A Theoretical Study of (Hyper) Self-Attention through the Lens of Interactions: Representation, Training, Generalization
papers.tldr: The paper explains how linear self-attention can learn pairwise interactions and introduces modules for richer feature and multi-entity dependencies.

papers.title: Ad-Hoc Human-AI Coordination Challenge

papers.title: AssistanceZero: Scalably Solving Assistance Games

papers.title: Boosting Virtual Agent Learning and Reasoning: A Step-Wise, Multi-Dimensional, and Generalist Reward Model with Benchmark
papers.tldr: Similar evaluates virtual-agent actions across five dimensions, supplying intermediate feedback for training and action selection at inference time.

papers.title: Craftium: Bridging Flexibility and Efficiency for Rich 3D Single- and Multi-Agent Environments

papers.title: DipLLM: Fine-Tuning LLM for Strategic Decision-making in Diplomacy

papers.title: Gravity-Bench-v1: A Benchmark on Gravitational Physics Discovery for Agents
papers.tldr: Gravity-Bench-v1 tests agents’ ability to discover hidden gravitational physics through budgeted experiments, including environments with unfamiliar physical rules.

papers.title: LARM: Large Auto-Regressive Model for Long-Horizon Embodied Intelligence
papers.tldr: LARM uses a large-language-model referee during reinforcement learning to train a smaller action model for long-horizon embodied tasks.

papers.title: Learning Strategic Language Agents in the Werewolf Game with Iterative Latent Space Policy Optimization
papers.tldr: LSPO improves Werewolf agents by alternating compact strategy-space optimization with language-model fine-tuning.

papers.title: MAGELLAN: Metacognitive predictions of learning progress guide autotelic LLM agents in large goal spaces
papers.tldr: MAGELLAN helps LLM agents choose productive goals by learning to predict their own competence and progress across related goals.

papers.title: PokéChamp: an Expert-level Minimax Language Agent

papers.title: Position: Truly Self-Improving Agents Require Intrinsic Metacognitive Learning
papers.tldr: The authors argue that self-improving agents need internal capacities to assess, plan, and revise how they learn.

papers.title: Sable: a Performant, Efficient and Scalable Sequence Model for MARL

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Pre-training Agents and World Models

papers.title: Training a Generally Curious Agent
papers.tldr: Paprika trains language models on diverse synthetic interactions so they can adapt their exploration to unseen tasks without further training.

papers.title: AlphaZero Neural Scaling and Zipf's Law: a Tale of Board Games and Power Laws

papers.title: Assembloid Agency: Unreal Engine API for brain-on-a-chip platforms
papers.tldr: Assembloid Agency proposes an Unreal Engine interface for designing interactive experiments with living neuronal cultures.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Master Complex Card Games?
papers.tldr: Supervised training can bring language models close to strong card-game AIs, with cross-game transfer and general capability retention depending on the training mix.

papers.title: Deep RL Needs Deep Behavior Analysis: Exploring Implicit Planning by Model-Free Agents in Open-Ended Environments

papers.title: EconGym: A Scalable AI Testbed with Diverse Economic Tasks

papers.title: EVAAA: A Virtual Environment Platform for Essential Variables in Autonomous and Adaptive Agents
papers.tldr: EVAAA provides virtual survival environments where embodied agents learn from internal physiological needs and face unseen tests of adaptation.

papers.title: Exploring Human-AI Conceptual Alignment through the Prism of Chess

papers.title: Generating Creative Chess Puzzles
papers.tldr: Reinforcement learning with chess-engine-derived rewards increases counter-intuitive puzzle generation and produces curated puzzles that experts rate highly for creativity.

papers.title: Ground-Compose-Reinforce: Grounding Language in Agentic Behaviours using Limited Data
papers.tldr: Ground-Compose-Reinforce uses compositional Reward Machines to learn complex agent behaviors from limited labeled trajectories.

papers.title: Gymnasium: A Standard Interface for Reinforcement Learning Environments
papers.tldr: Gymnasium standardizes reinforcement-learning environment interfaces and supplies tools that simplify experimentation, interoperability, and reproducibility.

papers.title: Heterogeneous Adversarial Play in Interactive Environments
papers.tldr: HAP co-trains a task-generating teacher and a problem-solving learner to produce adaptive curricula with competitive reported performance.

papers.title: Imagined Autocurricula

papers.title: Knowledge Starts with Practice: Knowledge-Aware Exercise Generative Recommendation with Adaptive Multi-Agent Cooperation
papers.tldr: ExeGen coordinates LLM agents to infer student knowledge from exercise responses and iteratively generate and refine personalized practice.

papers.title: MindForge: Empowering Embodied Agents with Theory of Mind for Lifelong Cultural Learning
papers.tldr: MindForge combines perspective taking, communication, and memory to help Minecraft agents learn from instruction and collaboration.

papers.title: PoE-World: Compositional World Modeling with Products of Programmatic Experts
papers.tldr: PoE-World combines LLM-generated programmatic experts to learn stochastic world models from few observations and support planning.

papers.title: RF-Agent: Automated Reward Function Design via Language Agent Tree Search

papers.title: SE-GUI: Enhancing Visual Grounding for GUI Agents via Self-Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: SE-GUI combines curated examples, dense accuracy feedback, and attention-guided refinement to improve interface grounding with 3,000 training samples.

papers.title: SimWorld: An Open-ended Simulator for Agents in Physical and Social Worlds

papers.title: Social World Model-Augmented Mechanism Design Policy Learning

papers.title: The Stochastic Parrot: a physical AI Cohabitant

papers.title: The World Is Bigger! A Computationally-Embedded Perspective on the Big World Hypothesis

papers.title: VAGEN: Reinforcing World Model Reasoning for Multi-Turn VLM Agents

papers.title: WALL-E: World Alignment by NeuroSymbolic Learning improves World Model-based LLM Agents
papers.tldr: WALL-E extracts executable environment knowledge from exploration and combines it with language-model planning to improve agent performance without reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Agent Learning via Early Experience
papers.tldr: Agents improve by learning from the future states produced by their own actions, even without reward signals.

papers.title: CooT: Learning to Coordinate In-Context with Coordination Transformers
papers.tldr: CooT learns to adapt to unfamiliar partners through observation and context, achieving rapid coordination without parameter updates.

papers.title: DECOR: Learning to Decompose and Collaborate in Deep Search via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: DECOR jointly trains planning, filtering, and answering agents to improve collaboration and performance in deep search.

papers.title: Designing Observation and Action Models for Efficient Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
papers.tldr: LOAM uses language models and adaptive candidate selection to design observation and action spaces that improve reinforcement learning.

papers.tldr: Reinforcement fine-tuning transfers well across task difficulty in familiar environments, but transfer to unseen environments is less reliable.

papers.title: Dreaming in Code for Curriculum Learning in Open-Ended Worlds
papers.tldr: Dreaming in Code generates executable environment variations that scaffold learning and improve long-horizon skill acquisition in Craftax.

papers.title: Lifting Traces to Logic: Programmatic Skill Induction with Neuro-Symbolic Learning for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

papers.title: Position: Behavioral Systems Require Behavioral Tests

papers.title: Position: Profiling Game Worlds by Transition Complexity

papers.title: Position: World Models as an Intermediary between Agents and the Real World

papers.tldr: PromptPilot coordinates multiple agents to optimize point prompts for frozen vision models, improving few-shot segmentation without inference-time parameter updates.

papers.title: TABX: A High-Throughput Sandbox Battle Simulator for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

papers.title: Unsupervised Partner Design Enables Robust Ad-hoc Teamwork

papers.title: What You Think is What You See: Driving Exploration in VLM Agents via Visual-Linguistic Curiosity
